title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent for DLP alerts reaches general availability
summary: Hold: the briefing implies administrators can configure the schedule, but Microsoft sets the schedule and only automatic versus manual execution is configurable. It also omits the Security Copilot owner role required to change overage capacity in that portal, omits the Teams app prerequisite for reminders, and describes the optional agent identity as unconditional in the risk rationale.

claims.claim: Deployment is reached in Microsoft Purview through Agents > Explore agents > Triage agent in Data Loss Prevention > View Details > Setup.
claims.quote:
In the left hand navigation pane, select **Agents**.
3. Select **Explore agents**.
4. On the card for the Triage agent in Data Loss Prevention, select **View Details** to open a page that shows the details about the agent.

claims.claim: Agent configuration is reached in Purview through Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration.
claims.quote:
select **Agents**.
2. Select **Explore agents**.

claims.claim: The Data Security Triage Agent is a Security Copilot agent embedded in Purview DLP.
claims.quote:
Microsoft Security Copilot agents are AI-powered processes that help you with specific role-based tasks. Microsoft Purview offers:

- [Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP)](dlp-learn-about-dlp) triage agent

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The agent reads content associated with DLP alerts.
claims.quote: Read file content and metadata involved in DLP alerts

claims.claim: The agent classifies alerts as Needs attention, Less urgent or Not categorized.
claims.quote:
The agent groups alerts into four categories:

- **All**
- **Needs attention**
- **Less urgent**
- **Not categorized**

claims.claim: The agent provides summaries explaining alert categorization.
claims.quote: The agent offers a comprehensive explanation for the logic behind the categorization.

claims.claim: Supported DLP policy locations are Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and devices.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview Triage Agent in DLP triages alerts from policies that are scoped to Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and devices (Endpoint) locations, *only*.

claims.claim: Only active-mode policies are supported, not simulation-mode policies.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP only supports alerts from policies that are in active mode. It doesn't triage alerts from DLP policies that are running in simulation mode.

claims.claim: Device alert triage requires evidence collection for file activities on devices.
claims.quote: To triage alerts from Devices, you must enable [evidence collection for file activities on devices](dlp-copy-matched-items-learn).

claims.claim: Files up to 2 MB are triaged.
claims.quote: Agents triage files up to 2 MB in size.

claims.claim: For alerts with 10 or more files, the agent summarizes the top 10.
claims.quote: When an alert includes 10 or more files, the agent uses the potentially top 10 files to generate the file risk summary.

claims.claim: Purview DLP results appear in the Alerts page's Triage Agent view.
claims.quote: Set the toggle to the **Triage Agent** view. This view shows agent triaged alerts.

claims.claim: Agent summaries also appear in the Defender XDR DLP alert queue.
claims.quote: Agent-provided summaries and risk factors will be available on DLP alerts triaged by the Agent as they are in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The agent can be deployed from either Purview or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals

claims.claim: Management, editing and disabling are only available in Purview.

claims.claim: Only one instance exists per tenant.
claims.quote: There can be only one instance of each agent in a tenant, regardless of the portal in which it was deployed.

claims.claim: The agent starts within 30-60 minutes after setup.
claims.quote: After setup is complete, the agent starts running within 30–60 minutes and begins triaging DLP alerts.

claims.claim: All DLP policies are in scope by default.
claims.quote: By default, the agent processes alerts from all DLP policies generated within the past 30 days.

claims.claim: The default alert look-back is 30 days.
